content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The bookmark manager specification is ready for review:

- [Specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)
- Feature directory: `specs/001-bookmark-manager`
- Validation: all checklist items passed; no unresolved clarifications

The draft assumes a private, single-user app supporting save, search, tags, sorting, editing, opening, and deletion. Accounts, sharing, imports, browser extensions, folders, and automatic page metadata are excluded from this initial release.

This draft follows the `speckit-specify` workflow and intentionally stops before planning or implementation.

Please approve the specification or describe any changes you want. Once approved, I’ll create the implementation plan.

Thanks for putting this together — a lot of it matches what I picture. Browsing my saved links with their titles, tags, and notes, searching them, filtering by tag, sorting, editing, opening, and deleting all sound right. But reading through your list of what's left out, several of those are things I really do want, so I can't approve it as-is yet.

A few things I'd like changed or added:

- **The app should fill in the details for me.** When I paste in a link, I don't want to type the title and description myself every time — I'd expect the app to go grab the page's title, its description, its little icon, and ideally a preview image automatically. I can then tweak any of that before or after saving if it got it wrong. You've got this listed as excluded, and that's actually one of the parts I care about most.

- **"Read it later" is missing entirely.** A big reason I save links is to come back and read them. I'd want to mark a link as unread/to-read, and be able to look at just my unread ones in their own place, then mark them read once I'm done so they drop off that list.

- **Archiving, separate from deleting.** Deleting for good is fine when I really mean it, but I'd also want to "put away" a link — hide it from my normal list and searches but keep it around in case I want it later. That's different from deletion, and I'd want a separate place to see the archived ones. Right now archiving is excluded and I'd like it back in.

- **Smarter searching.** Beyond plain text matching, I'd expect to search by tag with something like `#tagname`, to combine conditions (this AND that, one OR another, exclude something), and to search an exact phrase by putting it in quotes.

- **Doing things to several links at once.** When I'm tidying up, I'd want to select a bunch of links and, in one go, tag them, mark them read/unread, archive them, or delete them.

A couple of smaller things I'd also want eventually, though I'll let you tell me the right order: writing a longer formatted note on a link and having it show nicely when I view it; saving a search-plus-tag combination so I can reuse it later; bringing bookmarks in from a browser file and sending mine back out; and a few display preferences like default sort order and text size.

Could you revise the spec to bring these in — especially the automatic details, read-later, archiving, and the smarter search? Then I'll take another look.

content:
The specification has been revised and passes the quality checklist.

[Review the revised specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)  
[Review the validation checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)

Recommended delivery order:

1. P1 — automatic page details, smart search, and read-later
2. P2 — archiving, restoration, editing, and bulk actions
3. P3 — formatted notes and saved searches
4. P4 — browser import/export and display preferences

Notable defaults documented for review:

- New bookmarks start as unread.
- Opening a bookmark does not automatically mark it read.
- Archived bookmarks retain their read status but disappear from ordinary and unread views.
- Search supports `#tags`, quoted phrases, `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`/`-`, and parentheses.
- Imported browser folders become tags.
- Automatic metadata failures never prevent manual entry and saving.

The `speckit-specify` workflow guided this revision. No planning or implementation has begun. Please approve this version or flag anything else you’d like changed.

This is a big improvement — it really captures what I was after. The automatic page details, the read-later queue with those sensible defaults (starting unread, and not marking things read just because I opened them), archiving as its own reversible thing separate from deleting, the smarter search with tags and quotes and and/or/not and grouping, selecting a bunch at once to act on them, the formatted notes, the saved searches, and moving bookmarks in and out — all of that matches how I pictured using it. The defaults you called out sound right to me.

One thing I noticed you've set aside that I'd actually like included: keeping my own readable copy of a saved page. Pages I save sometimes go away, get paywalled, or change later, and I'd hate to lose the thing I saved a link for. So when I save a bookmark, I'd want the app to also keep a copy of that page as it looked, so I can still read it even if the original disappears. And in the case where the link points at a PDF rather than a normal web page, I'd expect it to just keep the PDF itself rather than a copy of a webpage.

Could you fold that in? Once that's in the spec I think we're good to move on to planning.

The offline-copy capability is now included as P1 scope in the revised [specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md).

It covers:

- Readable, visually recognizable offline captures of web pages
- Retention of the original file for PDF links
- Pending, available, and failed capture states
- Retry after failed captures
- Offline access when the source changes or disappears
- Preservation through archiving and restoration
- Explicit confirmation before deleting a retained copy
- Safe viewing without retained page scripts performing actions
- Background capture for imported bookmarks

The [quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md) passes all 16 items with no unresolved clarifications.

This revision followed `speckit-specify`. Please confirm the updated specification, and I’ll proceed to the implementation-plan gate.

That's exactly what I wanted — keeping a readable copy of the page, holding onto the actual file when it's a PDF, being able to still open my copy when the original's gone, keeping the copy through archiving, and warning me before it gets deleted all match how I'd expect it to work.

The whole spec now lines up with what I have in my head. I'm happy with it — please go ahead to the implementation plan.

content:
The implementation plan is ready for review.

- [Implementation plan](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md)
- [Technical research and decisions](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/research.md)
- [Data model](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/data-model.md)
- [API contract](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/openapi.yaml)
- [Search-language contract](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/search-grammar.md)
- [Saved-copy lifecycle](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/capture-lifecycle.md)
- [Validation guide](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/quickstart.md)

Key decisions include:

- A single deployable Node.js application with React, Fastify, SQLite/FTS5, and local content-addressed storage
- Durable background capture with restart recovery
- Immutable offline pages and byte-identical PDFs
- Layered SSRF protection and sandboxed offline viewing
- A dedicated search parser supporting the approved syntax
- Transactional bulk actions and browser imports
- Match-all behavior when multiple tag filters are selected
- Flat browser-compatible exports with explicit disclosure of fields that cannot be represented

The plan passed its governance checks, contains no unresolved clarifications, and the OpenAPI document passed semantic validation with only advisory warnings for read-only endpoints lacking artificial 4xx responses.

This plan was produced through `speckit-plan`. Please approve it or request changes; after approval, I’ll generate the dependency-ordered implementation tasks.

Honestly most of the technical choices there are over my head, and I'll trust you on those. What matters to me is that the plan builds the app the way we agreed — saving links with the details filled in automatically, the read-later queue, archiving that's separate from deleting, the smarter searching, acting on several at once, the notes, saved searches, moving bookmarks in and out, the display preferences, and keeping my own readable copy of each page (and the actual file for PDFs). It sounds like that's all accounted for.

Go ahead and put together the tasks.

content:
The complete bookmark manager is built and ready for review at [http://maker:4000/](http://maker:4000/).

It includes the full approved scope: automatic page details, read-later, advanced search, archiving, bulk actions, formatted notes, saved views, import/export, display preferences, rendered offline pages, original PDF retention, and explicit recapture replacement.

Verification passed:

- Lint, typecheck, and production build
- Dependency audit: 0 vulnerabilities
- Unit, integration, security, and performance suites
- 9 end-to-end browser journeys
- 10,000-bookmark search/import-export checks
- 500-item bulk-action threshold
- Byte-identical PDF capture
- Backup, restore, blob audit, and foreign-key checks

See the [validation report](/work/docs/validation-report.md) and [completed task list](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/tasks.md).

I had a proper poke around and it does what I hoped. I saved a couple of links and they landed in my library marked unread, just like we said. When I tried saving the same link twice it wouldn't let me make a duplicate. Searching works nicely — I found things by a tag with `#`, it didn't care about capitalization, and combining terms and excluding a word both behaved the way I'd want. Marking something read dropped it out of my read-later list but kept it in the library, and archiving a link tucked it away out of my main list and into the archive on its own, without deleting it. The read-later, archive, saved views, import/export, and preferences are all right there in front of me too, and it's got a lovely calm look to it.

This is the app I wanted. I'm really pleased with it — thank you. I know there were a few extras we talked about along the way as "someday" ideas, and I'm happy to leave those for a future round; nothing's missing from what we agreed on for this one.
